trigger: any projection failure, including a transient one, or a future v4
summary: The boot error log embedded a hard-coded DROP SCHEMA device_inventory_store CASCADE plus schema_meta DELETE and an UPDATE ... version = 2 recipe. On a transient failure (a dropped connection reaches the same branch) or once a v4 exists (a rolled-back binary, a half-migrated schema) it names a data-destroying action for the wrong situation; version = 2 would re-run v3 and v4 over a half-migrated schema. Raised independently by architect (HIGH), compliance-officer, security-guardian (NICE) and unhappy-path (UP-1). Derived BLOCKING (I4). FIXED in a20fc02e3: the log no longer names any destructive step, prints the table and SQLSTATE, separates 42P01/42703 (schema defect) from other failures (restart once), and points at the upgrade note; the recipe lives only in upgrading.md, scoped to dev/UAT.
classification_rationale: the diff claimed or did something the code or docs did not support

trigger: a future column change to a stored kind
summary: No guard fired when a registry column list changed: the obligation to NULL row_count/content_digest (or bump the digest prefix) was doc-only, so a column append with an ALTER but no NULLing would show false mismatches (or, worse, a same-count edit read as unchanged). FIXED in a20fc02e3: a non-Postgres test pins every table-backed kind column list and kSectionDigestPrefix = v1:, so a registry edit cannot land without meeting the rule.

trigger: a reader of the code or docs
summary: The v3 comment still described the old failure and a vague recreate-the-schema remedy; the FROZEN comment said the equivalence was recorded in the commit message (not durable); the changelog fragment lacked the issue number prefix and led with the mechanism; the ADR-0016 note on a column change omitted the migration. FIXED in a20fc02e3.

A projection is column presence only: a dropped primary key or cascading foreign key (ON CONFLICT upserts, delete_agent) passes it. Accepted design, documented in the playbook. Partly CLOSED in a20fc02e3 for the shipped literals: the schema test asserts the primary key and cascading FK of every child table; a live deployed database remains unchecked (runner drift detection, #7158).

trigger: a rolling upgrade running a v4 ALTER while a current replica restarts
summary: A probe SELECT takes ACCESS SHARE and can wait behind another replica ACCESS EXCLUSIVE ALTER (a future v4) on the same table; the runner advisory lock does not cover a replica already at the current version, so the wait lasts to statement_timeout and then boot is refused. Latent: no v4 exists. A bounded lock_timeout with a retry is a new behaviour with its own review surface (Gate 7 test 1), so it is split out rather than folded here.
classification_rationale: the diff claimed or did something the code or docs did not support

trigger: a dropped connection during the probes
summary: A transient probe failure refuses boot of the whole server. This is the same posture as every other store (a restart is the retry) and the migration-failure branch at the same site was already fatal; the misleading part (a destructive recipe) is fixed under g1-arch-F2. An in-process retry is not added: it is a new behaviour on a boot path shared by all stores.
classification_rationale: pre-existing posture shared with sibling stores; mitigation applied via the message

summary: This store is now the only one that classifies the failure by SQLSTATE; api_token_store, software_inventory_store, product_registry_store and update_registry log a fixed text and the raw PG error.
